back: A ReplicaSet keeps N identical pods but never updates existing ones. A Deployment manages one ReplicaSet per pod-template version to provide rolling updates and rollbacks.
maxSurge: how many pods above `replicas` may exist during a rollout (rounds up). maxUnavailable: how many below `replicas` may be unavailable (rounds down). Defaults 25%/25%.
How long a new pod must be Ready before it counts as available for rollout progress. Catches pods that crash shortly after starting.
The `Progressing` condition becomes False with reason `ProgressDeadlineExceeded` and `rollout status` exits non-zero. No automatic rollback.
`kubectl rollout status | history | undo [--to-revision=N] | pause | resume | restart deploy/<name>`
Two full Deployments with labels `color=blue`/`color=green`; switch traffic by patching the Service selector.
A stable and a canary Deployment sharing a label the Service selects; the replica ratio sets the approximate traffic split.
Stable ordinal names, stable per-pod DNS via a headless Service, per-pod PVCs from `volumeClaimTemplates`, ordered create/update/delete (by default).
A Service with `clusterIP: None`. DNS returns the pod IPs directly, and StatefulSet pods get records like `pod-0.svc-name.ns.svc.cluster.local`.
`updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.partition: N` only updates pods with ordinal ≥ N: a manual canary for stateful apps.
completions = successful pods needed; parallelism = pods at once; backoffLimit = retries before Failed (default 6).
Deletes a finished Job (and its pods) automatically after the given number of seconds.
`Allow` (overlap allowed, default), `Forbid` (skip if previous still running), `Replace` (kill previous, start new).
